historical_reviews.v3_1: Requires measured simultaneous component load and continuous platform safety telemetry rather than inferring burn-in from process completion.

original_test_intent: Sustain the approved CPU, memory, GPU and network burn-in workload for one hour while proving the host remains responsive and produces no unapproved tool, OS or BMC errors.
original_method: Identify the exact topology and licensed/validated tool profile, preserve baseline logs before any approved clear, run the one-hour multi-component workload under continuous thermal/power/fan/error monitoring, stop safely on anomaly, and retain complete logs and post-health evidence.
manual_activity: An engineer must approve the workload profile, thresholds, log-clear policy and service impact; the agent may run the exact approved tools and collectors while a human remains able to intervene.
required_inputs: Approved BurnInTest or equivalent package, version, license and profile
Per-component load targets and success thresholds
Maintenance window, workload clearance and recovery
Known-event policy and protected evidence path
safety_requirements: Do not substitute CPU/memory stress for full source coverage
Do not expose passwords or bypass host identity
Export complete logs before any clear
Continuously monitor all component and platform health
Stop on thermal/power/fan/ECC/GPU/network/BMC anomaly or lost telemetry
No automatic retry or hardware PASS claim
agent_execution_scope: Run the approved one-hour profile after confirmation
Monitor and abort against exact limits
Collect complete tool and platform evidence and report without final verdict
engineer_actions: Approve tool/license/profile, safety thresholds and any log clear

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not equivalent: fixed stress-ng CPU/memory/storage workers omit GPU and network, use unsafe SSH practices and discard most output with tail.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the reviewed pinned project BurnIn/full-stress implementation or an approved equivalent profile that explicitly targets every required component; parameters must be supplied from topology and policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: One-hour duration, CPU/memory/GPU/network full-load intent, 30/60-minute fields and error/stability criteria are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record per-component utilization and throughput plus thermal, power, fan, ECC, GPU and network health at fixed intervals for the full 3600 seconds with an interlocked abort.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds measurable load targets, immutable logs and hard safety thresholds.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; unlike the DeepSeek command, GPU and network remain required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Task Manager visuals may support but cannot replace topology-specific counters and complete error telemetry.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve specific vendor tools or load percentages, but every omitted component must be declared as uncovered rather than treated as full burn-in coverage.
expected_evidence: Approval, limits, workload state and complete pre-test logs
Full one-hour tool stdout/stderr and exit/cleanup status
Time-series CPU/memory/GPU/network load plus thermal/power/fan health
Complete OS/BMC/SEL/blackbox and component error deltas
No hang/blue screen and stable post-test inventory/reachability
Event disposition and no hardware PASS claim

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Source consistently requires one-hour full-component load and clean stability evidence; missing exact tool parameters are finite readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An approved package/profile, thresholds and maintenance plan can make the workflow executable without changing its semantics.

review_improvement: Rejects an under-scoped and unsafe command and replaces it with topology-bound full-component load, continuous safety gates and complete evidence retention.
independent_technical_reasoning: A one-hour burn-in is automatable only after tool coverage, topology and hard-stop limits are approved. Because it intentionally stresses multiple subsystems and may clear logs, package and user confirmation are mandatory.
